structure.title: 6.1-6.2 Main Results (Eligibility on Autonomy; Direct Impacts on Firm Outcomes)

observations.statement: States that the empirical strategy uses a difference-in-differences and event-study framework to estimate the impact of the earned-autonomy program on managerial decisions and firm outcomes.

Uses pre-program eligibility for autonomy as a proxy for treatment rather than actual receipt of autonomy, explicitly to avoid endogeneity from the government selecting which firms are granted autonomy.
observations.quote: to sidestep the endogeneity concerns around the government picking firms for autonomy

observations.statement: Argues that sector-linear trends interacted with year fixed effects absorb any differential growth of eligible firms' sectors, and points to event-study estimates of the pre-trend conditional on these controls.

Discusses the recent literature on bias in two-way fixed-effects estimators under staggered treatment timing and states that a heterogeneity-robust estimator is used for specifications where staggering is a concern.

Motivates the heterogeneity design with a theoretical claim that the value of autonomy to the manager is increasing in the gap between government and manager preferences, proxied empirically by pre-program dividend behavior.
Combines newly digitized data from the government's annual Public Enterprise Survey Reports with existing financial-statement sources covering the pre- and post-program period.
Defines the unit of observation as the firm-year for the universe of federally owned state-owned enterprises, later restricted to a balanced panel for the main regressions.
Links the digitized SOE data to a commercial firm-level database to obtain industry classification codes and to build a private-firm comparison sample used only for production-function estimation.

First documents differential firm exit between eligible and ineligible firms, then justifies restricting the main analysis to the balanced panel of firms that report data throughout the full sample window.
observations.locator: Section 6.2 Direct Impacts on Firm Outcomes

observations.statement: Reports the number of observations underlying each column directly beneath the coefficient row in every main regression table, with the count varying by outcome according to that variable's data-availability window.
Constructs value added, the primary firm-performance outcome, by subtracting expenditure on raw materials, power, and fuel from sales in the firm's financial statements.

Defines the treatment proxy as a binary pre-program eligibility indicator equal to one if a firm earned profits continuously and held positive net worth before the program's introduction, and zero otherwise.

Derives total factor productivity and markups from a Cobb-Douglas production-function estimation applied jointly to the SOE panel and a matched sample of private firms, justified by the small number of SOEs per sector.
States that outcome variables not already expressed as percentages are winsorized at extreme percentiles to limit the influence of outliers before estimation.

Constructs a baseline incentive-conflict proxy from whether a firm paid dividends in every profitable year before the program, and notes that an alternative continuous cutoff for the same proxy yields similar heterogeneity results.

Main outcome tables report firm fixed effects, year fixed effects, and sector-linear trends in the table note, together with the observation count and the dependent-variable mean, but do not report R-squared.
States in the table notes that standard errors are clustered at the firm level for the panel difference-in-differences regressions.

Reports R-squared for the cross-sectional regression of autonomy receipt on eligibility and notes that standard errors there are robust rather than clustered, consistent with one observation per firm.

Presents a single baseline specification per outcome in the main tables rather than a progression of columns adding controls, with alternative specifications instead reported in separate tables and sections.

Clusters standard errors at the firm level for the repeated firm-year panel regressions but does not include an explicit discussion of why that clustering level, rather than an alternative such as sector, is appropriate.

Uses heteroskedasticity-robust rather than clustered standard errors for the single cross-sectional regression of autonomy receipt on eligibility, consistent with there being only one observation per firm.

Reports year-by-year event-study estimates around the policy year as the pre-trend diagnostic for the main outcomes, welfare outcomes, and mechanism variables, all displayed as figures in the main text.

Reports a dedicated regression and cumulative-count figure showing that pre-program eligibility strongly predicts later receipt of autonomy, presented as the diagnostic support for using eligibility as a treatment proxy.
Uses capacity-utilization data for the manufacturing subsample as a placebo-style diagnostic intended to rule out differential demand shocks as an alternative explanation for the main results.
Analyzes differential firm exit by eligibility status as an attrition diagnostic before restricting the main analysis to the balanced panel of firms.
Reports a donut-style robustness check that drops firms exactly at the eligibility threshold on either side, to address concern that such firms could have lobbied to set the eligibility rule.
Compares pre-program-eligible firms that never received autonomy against ineligible firms to test whether eligibility alone, absent actual autonomy, affects outcomes.

Reports a generalized difference-in-differences specification that uses eligibility at any point in the sample rather than only pre-program eligibility, combined with the heterogeneity-robust estimator, as an alternative to the main design.

Restricts to firms whose autonomy tier could not have been earned through additional effort during the relevant period, to net out incentive effects of moving to a higher autonomy level from the main treatment effect.

States that further robustness checks on strategic profit reporting and on the subsample of firms with at least one profitable pre-program year are reported in the Supplemental Appendix rather than the main text.
Reports split-sample results by a theory-motivated baseline incentive-conflict proxy, presenting separate panels for firms with higher versus lower baseline conflict with the government.
States that additional heterogeneity results by firms' differential capacity to undertake capital expansion under the program's rules are reported in the Supplemental Appendix.
Uses capital assets and the wage bill, the two decision levers granted by the program, as intermediate outcomes to show that managers actively exercise the granted autonomy.

Uses separate regressions on government ownership share and on the probability of a board vacancy to rule out changes in ownership and managerial turnover as alternative explanations for the main results.
Acknowledges that a possible time-use channel for managers cannot be definitively ruled out because data on managerial time allocation are not available.

Interprets the value-added effect relative to the dependent-variable mean and in standard-deviation units, and benchmarks its magnitude against an unrelated firm-consulting intervention study, while noting the effect accrues gradually over a longer horizon.
observations.quote: in line with results from interventions such as

observations.statement: Offers an alternative magnitude interpretation by normalizing treatment effects relative to firms' pre-program average levels, with the underlying table placed in the Supplemental Appendix.

States that the policy setting does not allow separate identification of the effect of randomly or quasi-randomly assigning autonomy, nor disentangling the effect of each individual decision right granted by the program.

Flags that dynamic incentives to reach a higher autonomy tier could induce anticipation effects that shape the investment profile of treated firms, even though the reported results are net of a specific incentive channel.
Presents dynamic treatment-effect estimates as event-study figures with confidence-interval bars rather than reporting the full set of year-by-year coefficients as text or a table.
Table notes specify both the standard-error clustering approach and the sample period or missing-year coverage underlying each outcome column.
Presents summary statistics in a dedicated table with separate columns for the full sample and for the subsample of firms eligible before the program.
Refers to supplemental results using an alphanumeric appendix-table labeling convention distinct from the main-text roman-numeral table numbers.

Main regression tables report point estimates with standard errors in parentheses and do not use significance stars, with statistical significance instead discussed narratively in the surrounding text.
Previews the direction of the main empirical findings, including the effect on value added and the offsetting effects on outcomes valued by the government, within the introduction.

Orders the paper with institutional background and a theoretical framework preceding the data and empirical-strategy sections, so the identification argument is presented after the model that motivates it.
Places robustness checks and additional outcomes in a dedicated section that follows the main-results and mechanisms section rather than interleaving them with the main results.
Structures the introduction around paragraphs that position the paper's contribution relative to three distinct literatures before moving to the institutional section.

States that the replication package is deposited with a public repository DOI and that, because parts of the underlying data are restricted, the package includes a simulated or synthetic dataset that allows the code to run.
observations.quote: granted an exemption to publish parts of their data

observations.statement: Includes an editorial statement that the journal verified the code's ability to generate the tables and figures using the synthetic data and a simplified version of the code, while noting the synthetic results are not expected to match the paper's reported results.
States that the authors obtained an exemption to publish only part of the underlying administrative data because of restricted access or lack of republication rights.
Names the specific statistical software package used for the markup estimation step of the empirical strategy.

Frames the setting as one specific country's federally owned enterprises during a particular policy episode, and leaves open for future research whether comparable earned-autonomy programs elsewhere generate similar impacts.

concordance.paper_says: Main specification is described as an OLS difference-in-differences with firm and year fixed effects and sector-linear trends (equation 6); a footnote states that results are reported throughout using the heterogeneity-robust de Chaisemartin and d'Haultfoeuille (2020) estimator.
concordance.card_shows: Main regression script calls Stata's did_multiplegt_old command (de Chaisemartin-d'Haultfoeuille estimator, hdfe_ols engine) rather than a plain fixed-effects OLS regression.
concordance.note: Confirms the footnote's statement that the corrected estimator, not a plain TWFE OLS, is used even for the non-staggered main pre-program-eligibility specification.

concordance.paper_says: Equation (6) and every main table note state that regressions include firm fixed effects, year fixed effects, and 2-digit-sector linear trends.
concordance.card_shows: Card field fe is null (not recorded) for spec s1; the command line includes a trends_lin(nic2) option consistent with the sector-linear-trend term.
concordance.note: Card leaves fe unrecorded even though the did_multiplegt_old call carries a trends_lin argument matching the paper's stated sector-trend control.

concordance.paper_says: Table notes across the main results tables state that standard errors are clustered at the firm level.
concordance.card_shows: Card records se as clustered on variable 'co' for spec s1.

concordance.paper_says: Panel regressions use clustered standard errors; the single cross-sectional eligibility-to-autonomy regression instead uses heteroskedasticity-robust standard errors.
concordance.card_shows: Only one specification (s1, the clustered panel regression) is recorded in the card; the cross-sectional robust-SE specification has no corresponding card entry.

concordance.paper_says: Main analysis is restricted to the balanced panel of firms reporting data for the full sample period, after separately documenting differential exit.
concordance.card_shows: Design record d1 has sample/treatment fields unrecorded (role unknown, treatment null).

concordance.paper_says: No weighting scheme is described for the main regressions.
concordance.card_shows: Card records weights as null for spec s1.

concordance.paper_says: States the only time-varying control beyond fixed effects is a 2-digit-sector-specific linear trend.
concordance.card_shows: Command line includes trends_lin(nic2), a sector-code-based linear trend option, consistent with the paper's description.

concordance.paper_says: Describes event-study estimates spanning several pre-program and post-program years, used as the pre-trend diagnostic.
concordance.card_shows: Command line includes dynamic() and placebo() options generating dynamic and placebo event-study coefficients, and the recipe records two figures produced by this script.

concordance.paper_says: Main text does not name the specific robust_dynamic, average_effect, or longdiff_placebo estimation options as separate robustness checks.
concordance.card_shows: Command line invokes robust_dynamic, average_effect, longdiff_placebo, and covariances options as part of the estimator call.

concordance.paper_says: Describes the main difference-in-differences results and corresponding event-study figure as feeding the firm-outcomes results table.
concordance.card_shows: Card's outputs field for spec s1 is empty, though the recipe-level summary separately counts one table and two figures for this design.

concordance.paper_says: Describes primary data as digitized government survey reports merged with a commercial firm database, spanning both the pre- and post-program period.
concordance.card_shows: Card is built from a small number of code files read from the replication package's simulated-data folder and does not record the underlying data-source description.

concordance.paper_says: States the comparison group is firms that were not eligible for autonomy before the program began.
concordance.card_shows: Design record d1 leaves the treatment/comparison definition unrecorded.

gaps: No pre-registration, IRB, or ethics statement appears anywhere in the read text.
No explicit discussion of why the firm level, rather than an alternative such as sector, is the appropriate clustering level, or of whether the number of clusters is adequate.
No first-stage or weak-instrument statistics are reported; the paper does not use an instrumental-variables design.
No balance table comparing pre-program-eligible and ineligible firms on baseline observable characteristics was found in the main text.
No explicit stars or significance-threshold legend was found in any table note; significance is instead discussed narratively.

Supplemental Appendix A-C (containing the lettered appendix tables and the theoretical proof) are cited throughout but are a separate document not included in this text extraction, so their diagnostic and robustness content could not be read directly.

reading.note: Read the entire extracted text (title/abstract, introduction, institutional background, theoretical framework, data, empirical strategy, main results, mechanisms, additional results and robustness, conclusion, and references) end to end. Supplemental Appendices A-C (lettered tables A.1-A.10 and the Appendix B proof), referenced repeatedly for additional outcomes, alternative specifications, and the theorem proof, are a separate document not included in this 24-page text extraction and were not read.
